ImageDescription.value: One of the 52 basswood animals on the Pullen Park Carousel hand-carved by Salvatore Cernigliaro for the Pennsylvania Carousel Company, founded by Gustav Dentzel. This is an orange tiger with black stripes.  Its brown underblanket is brown trimmed in gold scallops.  An overblanket is red with yellow trim and is edged to look like flames.  A brown-haired nymph dressed in turquoise toga and holding two turquoise ribbons is carvedunder and slightly forward of the saddle. This is a static animal on the outermost ring of the carousel. It is posed in a standing stance. The carousel underwent restoration from 1977 to 1982 during which time the original factory paint was uncovered, documented and conserved. Each hard carved animal was restored to its exact Munsell Color System paint color preserving the original paint underneath a layer of shellac while enabling the animals to look just as they were originally painted.
